verdict.rationale: Codex documents in-agent install paths: `/plugins` opens a plugin browser where you install from a marketplace, then start a new session to use the bundled skills. `$skill-installer linear` installs curated skills by name, and `codex plugin marketplace add` adds marketplace sources. A hands-on probe installed a skill into `.agents/skills` with one `npx` command, and Codex scans that directory. missing for 10: hands-on verification that a first-party install (`/plugins` or `$skill-installer`) is active in the next Codex session.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install a skill collection with one documented command — a package-manager one-liner, CLI, or in-agent marketplace command — and it is active in my next session

citations.quote: In Codex CLI, enter `/plugins` to open the plugin browser. Install a plugin from a configured marketplace, then start a new session before using its bundled skills or tools.
Use `codex plugin marketplace add` to add and track a marketplace source instead of editing `config.toml` by hand.
Installed plugins can add skills and MCP tools to new chats.
Codex scans `.agents/skills` in every directory from your current working directory up to the repository root.
